answer: At the mill the sacks are weighed on the great scales before any flour leaves the door, and the miller writes the weight in chalk on the beam. Proof of miller sack via flour stone ledger is the weighing: a sack the miller fills only after 14 stones are ground, each stone turned by the miller himself. First comes the summit, weighed at the hopper; then the jade, weighed at the door; the echo is the beam itself, chalked by the miller's own hand. A cheat must weigh 19 false sacks and chalk 19 false beams, and the mill still grinds no flour for his name.
